import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Nakai conjecture

The Nakai conjecture (Y. Nakai, 1961) states that if $V$ is a complex algebraic variety
whose ring of differential operators is generated by the derivations it contains, then $V$
is smooth. The converse is a theorem of Grothendieck.

For an affine variety $V$ with coordinate ring $R$ (a reduced, finitely generated
$\mathbb{C}$-algebra), the ring of differential operators is Grothendieck's ring
$D(R) = \bigcup_n D^n(R) \subseteq \operatorname{End}_{\mathbb{C}}(R)$, where
$D^0(R) = R$ (acting by multiplication) and $\theta \in D^{n+1}(R)$ iff
$[\theta, a] \in D^n(R)$ for all $a \in R$. The hypothesis of the conjecture is that $D(R)$
is generated, as a ring, by $R = D^0(R)$ together with the derivations
$\operatorname{Der}_{\mathbb{C}}(R)$, that is,
$D(R) = R\langle \operatorname{Der}_{\mathbb{C}}(R) \rangle$.
(Generation by derivations alone, without $R$, is impossible unless $R = \mathbb{C}$, since every
product of derivations kills $1$.) Over $\mathbb{C}$, smoothness of $V$ is the same as $R$ being a
smooth $\mathbb{C}$-algebra, or equivalently a regular ring.

The variety is only required to be reduced, not irreducible, as in the literature; for instance
the known Stanley–Reisner case is reducible.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Nakai conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nakai_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in
  mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- Y. Nakai, *On the theory of differentials in commutative rings*,
  J. Math. Soc. Japan 13 (1961), 63–84.
- K. R. Mount, O. E. Villamayor, *On a conjecture of Y. Nakai*,
  Osaka J. Math. 10 (1973), 325–327.
- A. Schreiner, *On a conjecture of Nakai*, Arch. Math. 62 (1994), 506–512.
-/

blocks.code:
def IsDiffOp : ℕ → Module.End k R → Prop
  | 0, θ => ∀ a : R, ⁅θ, LinearMap.mulLeft k a⁆ = 0
  | n + 1, θ => ∀ a : R, IsDiffOp n ⁅θ, LinearMap.mulLeft k a⁆
blocks.docstring:
`IsDiffOp k R n θ` says that the `k`-linear endomorphism `θ` of the commutative `k`-algebra
`R` is a (Grothendieck) differential operator of order at most `n`.

The definition is inductive: `θ` has order at most `0` if it commutes with every multiplication
operator `LinearMap.mulLeft k a`, `a : R` (such `θ` are exactly the multiplication operators);
and `θ` has order at most `n + 1` if the commutator `⁅θ, LinearMap.mulLeft k a⁆` has order at
most `n` for every `a : R`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Derivation k R R` (only order-1 operators killing 1), `Module.End k R` / `LinearMap.mulLeft` (used as building blocks); searched Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib for 'differential operator', 'DifferentialOperator', 'Weyl' — nothing.
justification.name: NakaiConjecture.IsDiffOp
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of (Grothendieck) differential operators of order ≤ n on a commutative algebra; `IsDiffOp k R n θ` is the standard inductive definition via iterated commutators with multiplication operators.

blocks.name: IsDiffOp
blocks.text:
/-- `IsDiffOp k R n θ` says that the `k`-linear endomorphism `θ` of the commutative `k`-algebra
`R` is a (Grothendieck) differential operator of order at most `n`.

The definition is inductive: `θ` has order at most `0` if it commutes with every multiplication
operator `LinearMap.mulLeft k a`, `a : R` (such `θ` are exactly the multiplication operators);
and `θ` has order at most `n + 1` if the commutator `⁅θ, LinearMap.mulLeft k a⁆` has order at

def IsDiffOp : ℕ → Module.End k R → Prop

  | n + 1, θ => ∀ a : R, IsDiffOp n ⁅θ, LinearMap.mulLeft k a⁆

blocks.code:
def diffOps : Set (Module.End k R) :=
  {θ | ∃ n, IsDiffOp k R n θ}
blocks.docstring:
The ring of differential operators `D(R)` of the commutative `k`-algebra `R`, as a subset of
`Module.End k R`: the `k`-linear endomorphisms of `R` that are differential operators of some
finite order.

justification.closest_existing_considered: No subalgebra of differential operators exists in Mathlib; a `Subalgebra` structure would require proving Grothendieck's closure lemma, so a `Set` is used.
justification.name: NakaiConjecture.diffOps
justification.why_needed: The ring of differential operators D(R) as the set `{θ | ∃ n, IsDiffOp k R n θ}` ⊆ `Module.End k R`, needed to state 'D(R) is generated by ...'.

blocks.name: diffOps

blocks.docstring:
The subset of `Module.End k R` consisting of the multiplication operators
`LinearMap.mulLeft k a`, `a : R`, together with the `k`-derivations of `R`. The `k`-subalgebra
of `Module.End k R` generated by this set is the ring `R⟨Der_k(R)⟩` of operators generated by

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Algebra.lmul k R` (range of multiplication operators) and `Derivation k R R`; no existing bundled set of both.
justification.name: NakaiConjecture.mulLeftsAndDerivations
justification.why_needed: The generating set `range (LinearMap.mulLeft k) ∪ range Derivation.toLinearMap` ⊆ `Module.End k R`, so that `Algebra.adjoin k` of it is the ring R⟨Der_k(R)⟩ generated by R and its derivations.

blocks.name: mulLeftsAndDerivations
blocks.text:
/-- The subset of `Module.End k R` consisting of the multiplication operators
`LinearMap.mulLeft k a`, `a : R`, together with the `k`-derivations of `R`. The `k`-subalgebra
of `Module.End k R` generated by this set is the ring `R⟨Der_k(R)⟩` of operators generated by
`R` and its derivations. -/
def mulLeftsAndDerivations : Set (Module.End k R) :=
  Set.range (LinearMap.mulLeft k : R → Module.End k R) ∪
    Set.range (fun D : Derivation k R R ↦ D.toLinearMap)

@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem isDiffOp_zero_op (n : ℕ) : IsDiffOp k R n (0 : Module.End k R) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => intro a; simp
  | succ n ih => intro a; simpa using ih
blocks.docstring: The zero operator has order at most `n` for every `n`.
blocks.name: isDiffOp_zero_op

theorem isDiffOp_zero_op (n : ℕ) : IsDiffOp k R n (0 : Module.End k R) := by

  | zero => intro a; simp
  | succ n ih => intro a; simpa using ih

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem IsDiffOp.succ {n : ℕ} {θ : Module.End k R} (h : IsDiffOp k R n θ) :
    IsDiffOp k R (n + 1) θ := by
  induction n generalizing θ with
  | zero => intro a; rw [h a]; exact isDiffOp_zero_op 0
  | succ n ih => intro a; exact ih (h a)
blocks.docstring: A differential operator of order at most `n` has order at most `n + 1`.
blocks.name: IsDiffOp.succ
blocks.text:

@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem IsDiffOp.succ {n : ℕ} {θ : Module.End k R} (h : IsDiffOp k R n θ) :
    IsDiffOp k R (n + 1) θ := by
  induction n generalizing θ with
  | zero => intro a; rw [h a]; exact isDiffOp_zero_op 0
  | succ n ih => intro a; exact ih (h a)

  intro b
  ext c
  simp [Ring.lie_def, mul_left_comm]
blocks.docstring: Multiplication by an element of `R` is a differential operator of order `0`.

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem isDiffOp_zero_iff_exists_mulLeft (θ : Module.End k R) :
    IsDiffOp k R 0 θ ↔ ∃ a : R, θ = LinearMap.mulLeft k a := by
  refine ⟨fun h ↦ ⟨θ 1, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · ext b
    have := LinearMap.congr_fun (h b) 1
    simpa [Ring.lie_def, mul_comm, sub_eq_zero] using this
  · rintro ⟨a, rfl⟩
    exact isDiffOp_zero_mulLeft a
blocks.docstring: The differential operators of order `0` are exactly the multiplication operators.
blocks.name: isDiffOp_zero_iff_exists_mulLeft

  · rintro ⟨a, rfl⟩

@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem lie_derivation_mulLeft (D : Derivation k R R) (a : R) :
    ⁅D.toLinearMap, LinearMap.mulLeft k a⁆ = LinearMap.mulLeft k (D a) := by
  ext b
  simp [Ring.lie_def, D.leibniz, mul_comm]
blocks.docstring: The commutator of a derivation `D` with multiplication by `a` is multiplication by `D a`.
blocks.name: lie_derivation_mulLeft

    ⁅D.toLinearMap, LinearMap.mulLeft k a⁆ = LinearMap.mulLeft k (D a) := by
  ext b
  simp [Ring.lie_def, D.leibniz, mul_comm]

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem isDiffOp_one_derivation (D : Derivation k R R) : IsDiffOp k R 1 D.toLinearMap := by
  intro a
  rw [lie_derivation_mulLeft]
  exact isDiffOp_zero_mulLeft _
blocks.docstring: A derivation is a differential operator of order at most `1`.
blocks.name: isDiffOp_one_derivation

theorem isDiffOp_one_derivation (D : Derivation k R R) : IsDiffOp k R 1 D.toLinearMap := by
  intro a
  rw [lie_derivation_mulLeft]
  exact isDiffOp_zero_mulLeft _

@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem mulLeftsAndDerivations_subset_diffOps : mulLeftsAndDerivations k R ⊆ diffOps k R := by
  rintro θ (⟨a, rfl⟩ | ⟨D, rfl⟩)
  · exact ⟨0, isDiffOp_zero_mulLeft a⟩
  · exact ⟨1, isDiffOp_one_derivation D⟩
blocks.docstring: The multiplication operators and the derivations are differential operators.
blocks.name: mulLeftsAndDerivations_subset_diffOps
blocks.text:

theorem mulLeftsAndDerivations_subset_diffOps : mulLeftsAndDerivations k R ⊆ diffOps k R := by
  rintro θ (⟨a, rfl⟩ | ⟨D, rfl⟩)
  · exact ⟨0, isDiffOp_zero_mulLeft a⟩
  · exact ⟨1, isDiffOp_one_derivation D⟩

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 13]
theorem diffOps_self_eq_adjoin_mulLeftsAndDerivations :
    diffOps k k = (Algebra.adjoin k (mulLeftsAndDerivations k k) : Set (Module.End k k)) := by
  apply Set.eq_of_subset_of_subset
  · intro θ _
    rw [end_self_eq_mulLeft θ]
    exact Algebra.subset_adjoin (Or.inl ⟨_, rfl⟩)
  · intro θ _
    exact ⟨0, end_self_eq_mulLeft θ ▸ isDiffOp_zero_mulLeft (θ 1)⟩
blocks.docstring:
Sanity check: for the base ring itself (the coordinate ring of a point), the ring of
differential operators is generated by the multiplication operators and the derivations.
blocks.name: diffOps_self_eq_adjoin_mulLeftsAndDerivations
blocks.text:
/-- Sanity check: for the base ring itself (the coordinate ring of a point), the ring of
differential operators is generated by the multiplication operators and the derivations. -/
@[category test, AMS 13]
theorem diffOps_self_eq_adjoin_mulLeftsAndDerivations :
    diffOps k k = (Algebra.adjoin k (mulLeftsAndDerivations k k) : Set (Module.End k k)) := by
  apply Set.eq_of_subset_of_subset
  · intro θ _
    rw [end_self_eq_mulLeft θ]
    exact Algebra.subset_adjoin (Or.inl ⟨_, rfl⟩)
  · intro θ _
    exact ⟨0, end_self_eq_mulLeft θ ▸ isDiffOp_zero_mulLeft (θ 1)⟩
end DifferentialOperators

@[category research open, AMS 13 14]
theorem nakai_conjecture (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [Algebra ℂ R] [Algebra.FiniteType ℂ R]
    [IsReduced R]
    (h : diffOps ℂ R =
      (Algebra.adjoin ℂ (mulLeftsAndDerivations ℂ R) : Set (Module.End ℂ R))) :
    Algebra.Smooth ℂ R := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:

$R$, i.e. $R$ is a reduced, finitely generated $\mathbb{C}$-algebra. If the ring of differential
operators $D(R)$ of $V$ is generated by the derivations it contains, i.e. $D(R)$ is the
$\mathbb{C}$-subalgebra of $\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb{C}}(R)$ generated by the multiplication
operators $R = D^0(R)$ and the derivations $\operatorname{Der}_{\mathbb{C}}(R)$, then $V$ is

claims.decomposer_note: Single universally quantified implication: for every (affine, reduced) complex algebraic variety V with coordinate ring R (a finitely generated reduced ℂ-algebra), if Grothendieck's ring of differential operators D(R) is generated as an R-algebra by R = D^0(R) and the derivations Der_ℂ(R) (equivalently, every order-n operator is a sum of products of ≤ n derivations), then V is smooth, i.e. R is regular; Mathlib lacks D(R), so a helper definition of differential operators of order ≤ n (via iterated commutators with multiplication maps) would be needed, and the converse (Grothendieck), the known special cases (curves, Stanley–Reisner rings) and the Zariski–Lipman consequence mentioned in the article are not posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same reading (affine reduced finite-type ℂ-algebra R; Grothendieck's D(R) ⊆ End_ℂ(R) via iterated commutators with multiplication operators; hypothesis D(R) = R⟨Der_ℂ(R)⟩; conclusion Algebra.Smooth ℂ R), and I verified that their different spellings of the multiplication operator (LinearMap.mulLeft / Algebra.lmul / Algebra.lsmul / LinearMap.mul) and of the commutator (⁅·,·⁆ vs P*Q-Q*P) are definitionally equal, and that the two order-0 conventions (∃ r, θ = mulLeft r vs commuting with all mulLeft) are provably equivalent (proved in c03/c05/c08 and in the final file). c07 alone uses the filtered variant (order-≤n operators lie in the R-span of words of ≤n derivations); that is a stronger hypothesis than the literal 'ring generated by derivations', so the ring-generation candidates are the more literal formalization of the source sentence. Among the equivalent ring-generation candidates, c06 has the fullest bespoke-definition API (order-0 characterization, derivations have order ≤1, filtration monotone, generators lie in D(R)) plus a test showing the hypothesis is satisfiable for R = k, as CONTRIBUTING.md requests for bespoke definitions. Edits: hypothesis written as diffOps ℂ R = ↑(Algebra.adjoin ℂ …) (D(R) = R⟨Der⟩ direction), standard binder order, added the ∃-mulLeft characterization of order 0, docstring notes on why R must be among the generators and on reduced-vs-irreducible, line-length fixes.

context:
In mathematics, the Nakai conjecture is an unproven characterization of smooth algebraic varieties, conjectured by Japanese mathematician Yoshikazu Nakai in 1961.
It states that if V is a complex algebraic variety, such that its ring of differential operators is generated by the derivations it contains, then V is a smooth variety. The converse statement, that smooth algebraic varieties have rings of differential operators that are generated by their derivations, is a result of Alexander Grothendieck.
The Nakai conjecture is known to be true for algebraic curves and Stanley–Reisner rings. A proof of the conjecture would also establish the Zariski–Lipman conjecture, for a complex variety V with coordinate ring R. This conjecture states that if the derivations of R are a free module over R, then V is smooth.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single slot matches the statement; its notes (affine reduced finitely generated ℂ-algebra, Grothendieck's D(R), generation as an R-algebra by derivations, smooth = regular, helper definition via iterated commutators) were followed.

namespace NakaiConjecture

section DifferentialOperators

variable (k R : Type*) [CommRing k] [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]

/-- `IsDiffOp k R n θ` says that the `k`-linear endomorphism `θ` of the commutative `k`-algebra
`R` is a (Grothendieck) differential operator of order at most `n`.

The definition is inductive: `θ` has order at most `0` if it commutes with every multiplication
operator `LinearMap.mulLeft k a`, `a : R` (such `θ` are exactly the multiplication operators);
and `θ` has order at most `n + 1` if the commutator `⁅θ, LinearMap.mulLeft k a⁆` has order at
most `n` for every `a : R`. -/
def IsDiffOp : ℕ → Module.End k R → Prop
  | 0, θ => ∀ a : R, ⁅θ, LinearMap.mulLeft k a⁆ = 0
  | n + 1, θ => ∀ a : R, IsDiffOp n ⁅θ, LinearMap.mulLeft k a⁆

/-- The ring of differential operators `D(R)` of the commutative `k`-algebra `R`, as a subset of
`Module.End k R`: the `k`-linear endomorphisms of `R` that are differential operators of some
finite order. -/
def diffOps : Set (Module.End k R) :=
  {θ | ∃ n, IsDiffOp k R n θ}

/-- The subset of `Module.End k R` consisting of the multiplication operators
`LinearMap.mulLeft k a`, `a : R`, together with the `k`-derivations of `R`. The `k`-subalgebra
of `Module.End k R` generated by this set is the ring `R⟨Der_k(R)⟩` of operators generated by
`R` and its derivations. -/
def mulLeftsAndDerivations : Set (Module.End k R) :=
  Set.range (LinearMap.mulLeft k : R → Module.End k R) ∪
    Set.range (fun D : Derivation k R R ↦ D.toLinearMap)

variable {k R}

@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem isDiffOp_zero_iff (θ : Module.End k R) :
    IsDiffOp k R 0 θ ↔ ∀ a : R, ⁅θ, LinearMap.mulLeft k a⁆ = 0 :=
  Iff.rfl

@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem isDiffOp_succ_iff (n : ℕ) (θ : Module.End k R) :
    IsDiffOp k R (n + 1) θ ↔ ∀ a : R, IsDiffOp k R n ⁅θ, LinearMap.mulLeft k a⁆ :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- The zero operator has order at most `n` for every `n`. -/
@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem isDiffOp_zero_op (n : ℕ) : IsDiffOp k R n (0 : Module.End k R) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => intro a; simp
  | succ n ih => intro a; simpa using ih

/-- A differential operator of order at most `n` has order at most `n + 1`. -/
@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem IsDiffOp.succ {n : ℕ} {θ : Module.End k R} (h : IsDiffOp k R n θ) :
    IsDiffOp k R (n + 1) θ := by
  induction n generalizing θ with
  | zero => intro a; rw [h a]; exact isDiffOp_zero_op 0
  | succ n ih => intro a; exact ih (h a)

/-- Multiplication by an element of `R` is a differential operator of order `0`. -/
@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem isDiffOp_zero_mulLeft (a : R) : IsDiffOp k R 0 (LinearMap.mulLeft k a) := by
  intro b
  ext c
  simp [Ring.lie_def, mul_left_comm]

/-- The differential operators of order `0` are exactly the multiplication operators. -/
@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem isDiffOp_zero_iff_exists_mulLeft (θ : Module.End k R) :
    IsDiffOp k R 0 θ ↔ ∃ a : R, θ = LinearMap.mulLeft k a := by
  refine ⟨fun h ↦ ⟨θ 1, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · ext b
    have := LinearMap.congr_fun (h b) 1
    simpa [Ring.lie_def, mul_comm, sub_eq_zero] using this
  · rintro ⟨a, rfl⟩
    exact isDiffOp_zero_mulLeft a

/-- The commutator of a derivation `D` with multiplication by `a` is multiplication by `D a`. -/
@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem lie_derivation_mulLeft (D : Derivation k R R) (a : R) :
    ⁅D.toLinearMap, LinearMap.mulLeft k a⁆ = LinearMap.mulLeft k (D a) := by
  ext b
  simp [Ring.lie_def, D.leibniz, mul_comm]

/-- A derivation is a differential operator of order at most `1`. -/
@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem isDiffOp_one_derivation (D : Derivation k R R) : IsDiffOp k R 1 D.toLinearMap := by
  intro a
  rw [lie_derivation_mulLeft]
  exact isDiffOp_zero_mulLeft _

/-- The multiplication operators and the derivations are differential operators. -/
@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem mulLeftsAndDerivations_subset_diffOps : mulLeftsAndDerivations k R ⊆ diffOps k R := by
  rintro θ (⟨a, rfl⟩ | ⟨D, rfl⟩)
  · exact ⟨0, isDiffOp_zero_mulLeft a⟩
  · exact ⟨1, isDiffOp_one_derivation D⟩

/-- Every `k`-linear endomorphism of `k` is a multiplication operator. -/
@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem end_self_eq_mulLeft (θ : Module.End k k) : θ = LinearMap.mulLeft k (θ 1) := by
  ext
  simp

/-- Sanity check: for the base ring itself (the coordinate ring of a point), the ring of
differential operators is generated by the multiplication operators and the derivations. -/
@[category test, AMS 13]
theorem diffOps_self_eq_adjoin_mulLeftsAndDerivations :
    diffOps k k = (Algebra.adjoin k (mulLeftsAndDerivations k k) : Set (Module.End k k)) := by
  apply Set.eq_of_subset_of_subset
  · intro θ _
    rw [end_self_eq_mulLeft θ]
    exact Algebra.subset_adjoin (Or.inl ⟨_, rfl⟩)
  · intro θ _
    exact ⟨0, end_self_eq_mulLeft θ ▸ isDiffOp_zero_mulLeft (θ 1)⟩

end DifferentialOperators

/-- **Nakai conjecture.** Let $V$ be a complex (affine) algebraic variety with coordinate ring
$R$, i.e. $R$ is a reduced, finitely generated $\mathbb{C}$-algebra. If the ring of differential
operators $D(R)$ of $V$ is generated by the derivations it contains, i.e. $D(R)$ is the
$\mathbb{C}$-subalgebra of $\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb{C}}(R)$ generated by the multiplication
operators $R = D^0(R)$ and the derivations $\operatorname{Der}_{\mathbb{C}}(R)$, then $V$ is
smooth, i.e. $R$ is a smooth $\mathbb{C}$-algebra. -/
@[category research open, AMS 13 14]
theorem nakai_conjecture (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [Algebra ℂ R] [Algebra.FiniteType ℂ R]
    [IsReduced R]
    (h : diffOps ℂ R =
      (Algebra.adjoin ℂ (mulLeftsAndDerivations ℂ R) : Set (Module.End ℂ R))) :
    Algebra.Smooth ℂ R := by
  sorry

end NakaiConjecture

items: 'Complex algebraic variety' is modelled by its coordinate ring: an affine variety with R a reduced, finitely generated ℂ-algebra (`[IsReduced R] [Algebra.FiniteType ℂ R]`). Irreducibility (integral domain) is NOT imposed, matching the literature (Mount–Villamayor, Schreiner, Traves state it for reduced finitely generated algebras; the Stanley–Reisner case cited in the article is non-irreducible). The affine setting is the standard one for 'the ring of differential operators'; for non-affine varieties the condition is local, so this is the faithful reading.

'Ring of differential operators' is Grothendieck's D(R) = ⋃ₙ Dⁿ(R) ⊆ End_ℂ(R), with D⁰(R) = {θ : [θ, a] = 0 ∀ a} (= multiplication operators) and Dⁿ⁺¹(R) = {θ : [θ, a] ∈ Dⁿ(R) ∀ a ∈ R}, where a acts by `LinearMap.mulLeft ℂ a`. Operators are ℂ-linear (D_{R/ℂ}).

'Generated by its contained derivations' is read as: D(R) is generated as a ring by R = D⁰(R) together with Der_ℂ(R), i.e. D(R) = R⟨Der_ℂ(R)⟩ (equivalently D(R) is generated by D¹(R) = R ⊕ Der_ℂ(R), Nakai's formulation). Literal generation by derivations alone (without R) is impossible even for smooth R, since all products of derivations kill constants while multiplication by non-scalars does not. Formalized as equality of sets `(Algebra.adjoin ℂ (mulLeftsAndDerivations ℂ R) : Set _) = diffOps ℂ R`; the inclusion ⊆ always holds (Grothendieck), so this is equivalent to D(R) ⊆ R⟨Der⟩.

'Smooth' is formalized as `Algebra.Smooth ℂ R` (formally smooth + finitely presented). For finite-type algebras over the perfect field ℂ this is equivalent to R being regular, which is the conclusion in Nakai's conjecture. Mathlib has no `IsRegularLocalRing`/regular-ring predicate in this checkout, and smoothness is in any case what the statement literally says.

Boundary: R = 0 (empty variety) satisfies both hypothesis and conclusion (`Algebra.Smooth ℂ 0` holds), so no `Nontrivial R` hypothesis is needed. The hypothesis is satisfiable (proved in-file for R = k as a `test`; holds for polynomial rings by Grothendieck), so the statement is not vacuous.

The helper definitions are stated over a general commutative ring k (the conjecture theorem itself is over ℂ). Basic API lemmas (multiplication operators have order 0, derivations have order ≤ 1, Dⁿ ⊆ Dⁿ⁺¹, generators lie in D(R)) are proved, not sorried.

reviewer_notes: Modeling choices a reviewer should know: (1) 'Complex algebraic variety' is taken as affine and represented by its coordinate ring R, a finitely generated reduced ℂ-algebra; irreducibility is not imposed, matching Mount–Villamayor/Schreiner/Traves and the reducible Stanley–Reisner case mentioned in the article (adding IsDomain would only weaken the conjecture). (2) 'Generated by its contained derivations' cannot mean the ℂ-algebra generated by derivations alone (every product of derivations kills 1, so it never contains multiplication by a non-scalar); it is formalized as D(R) = the ℂ-subalgebra of End_ℂ(R) generated by the multiplication operators R = D⁰(R) and Der_ℂ(R), i.e. generation as an R-algebra / as a ring by D¹(R). Since D(R) is a subring containing the generators, the equality is equivalent to D(R) ⊆ R⟨Der⟩. (3) The filtered variant Dⁿ(R) = Σ_{m≤n} R·Derᵐ (c07) is a priori a stronger hypothesis; the literal source sentence is ring generation, so it was not used. (4) 'Smooth' is Algebra.Smooth ℂ R (formally smooth + finitely presented); for finite type algebras over the perfect field ℂ this is equivalent to R being regular, and Mathlib has no regular-ring predicate in this checkout. (5) Boundary case: R = 0 satisfies the hypothesis (D(0) = {0} = adjoin) and Algebra.Smooth ℂ 0 holds, so no Nontrivial hypothesis is needed; the hypothesis is satisfiable (R = ℂ proved in-file; polynomial rings by Grothendieck), so the statement is not vacuous. No candidate omitted the slot; the confidence figures (0.85–0.97) were consistent with the Lean text. Final file also passes `lake --wfail build` when placed in FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/.
statement: Nakai conjecture: if a complex algebraic variety has a ring of differential operators generated by its contained derivations, then it must be smooth.
